claim.pdf_says: In the 13.18.60.2 USAGE clause general format, the four brace groups 'BINARY-CHAR { SIGNED / UNSIGNED }', 'BINARY-SHORT { SIGNED / UNSIGNED }', 'BINARY-LONG { SIGNED / UNSIGNED }' and 'BINARY-DOUBLE { SIGNED / UNSIGNED }' print SIGNED WITHOUT an underline and UNSIGNED WITH an underline. Verified on the 300 dpi render of page 533 and again on a 5x tight crop of the BINARY-CHAR brace (E:/Temp/specrecon/f4/crop_533_900_620.png): no rule under 'SIGNED', a full-width rule under 'UNSIGNED'. The same asymmetry repeats in all four rows.
claim.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md, page-533 figure notes: "> **Figure notes (USAGE clause general format).** Underlined in the printed standard (required words / required minimum abbreviation): `USAGE`, `BINARY`, `BINARY-CHAR`, `BINARY-SHORT`, `BINARY-LONG`, `BINARY-DOUBLE`, `SIGNED`, `UNSIGNED`, `BIT`, ... `IS`, `OF`, `TO`, and `WITH` are not underlined." — SIGNED is listed among the underlined (required) words.
claim.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.6.2/5.2.6.3, an underlined uppercase word is a REQUIRED word and a non-underlined uppercase word is an OPTIONAL word that may be omitted without changing the meaning. Because SIGNED is printed unmarked, the brace group '{ SIGNED / UNSIGNED }' is satisfiable by writing nothing at all, so USAGE BINARY-CHAR, USAGE BINARY-CHAR SIGNED and USAGE BINARY-CHAR UNSIGNED are all legal (likewise -SHORT, -LONG, -DOUBLE). Promoting SIGNED to a required word makes the brace a mandatory two-way choice, which rejects the bare 'USAGE BINARY-CHAR' / 'USAGE BINARY-LONG' spellings that real COBOL source uses constantly. This is the same falsely-restrictive direction of loss the sweep is hunting: legal source made to look illegal. A compiler or reviewer working from this note would emit a diagnostic for conforming source and mis-classify SIGNED as a required word rather than an optional word.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED, independently, by re-rendering page 533 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v533/spec_p533.png, 2550x3300) and inspecting the glyphs directly rather than trusting the OCR text layer.

(1) WHAT THE PRINTED GLYPHS ACTUALLY SHOW. At 3x-4x magnification of each brace group (crops written to E:/Temp/specrecon/v533/crop_char.png, crop_short.png, crop_long.png, crop_double.png) the asymmetry is unmistakable and repeats in all four rows: the head word (BINARY-CHAR / BINARY-SHORT / BINARY-LONG / BINARY-DOUBLE) carries a full-width rule, UNSIGNED carries a full-width rule, and SIGNED carries NO rule at all. There is clear white space between the SIGNED baseline and the top of the UNSIGNED cap-height in every row.

(2) QUANTITATIVE CONFIRMATION, to rule out a faint or hairline rule lost to anti-aliasing. Scanning each candidate underline band for rows where >=60% of the horizontal extent is dark: the UNSIGNED band produces a 2-pixel rule at 0.91 dark fraction in every one of the four rows (y=732, 882, 1031, 1181). The SIGNED band produces NOTHING above threshold in any row; its maximum is 0.47 / 0.49 / 0.54 / 0.51, and those maxima land exactly on the glyph baseline row where the serifs and stem feet of S-I-G-N-E-D sit, not on a continuous rule. A real underline in this document renders at 0.91; SIGNED never exceeds 0.54. The distinction is not marginal.

(3) THE MARKDOWN QUOTE IS ACCURATE, NOT A MISQUOTE. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 22406 reads verbatim as claimed: it lists `SIGNED` inside the underlined/required-word enumeration and then closes with "`IS`, `OF`, `TO`, and `WITH` are not underlined" — an exhaustive-sounding negative list that positively excludes SIGNED from the optional words. So the note asserts the opposite of the print in two independent places.

(4) THE LOSS IS NOT RECOVERABLE FROM ELSEWHERE IN THE TRANSCRIPTION. The ASCII figure in the code fence (lines 22370-22380) carries no underlining whatsoever — plain-text braces and words only. The figure note is therefore the SOLE carrier of the required/optional distinction for this format in the markdown. A wrong note is not a cosmetic annotation error here; it is the entire normative signal.

(5) THE SEMANTIC CONSEQUENCE IS REAL AND IS EXACTLY THE FALSELY-RESTRICTIVE DIRECTION. 5.2.2 Keywords: "They are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required...". 5.2.3 Optional words: "They are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats." 8.9 (line 5805): "Within each format, uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics of the format." And decisively, 5.2.6.3 Braces: "If one of the alternatives contains only optional words, that alternative is the default and is selected unless another alternative is explicitly specified." The SIGNED alternative contains ONLY optional words, so it is the default and is implicitly selected — which is precisely why bare `USAGE BINARY-CHAR` / `BINARY-SHORT` / `BINARY-LONG` / `BINARY-DOUBLE` is legal and signed. The note as written makes the brace a mandatory two-way choice and would reject the bare spellings, which are ubiquitous in real source.

(6) CORROBORATED BY THE SURROUNDING NORMATIVE TEXT. GR 21 (line 22619) speaks of "a data item described with the SIGNED phrase" versus "the UNSIGNED phrase" as a phrase-level distinction, and the minimum-range table (lines 22536-22543) pairs BINARY-CHAR SIGNED against BINARY-CHAR UNSIGNED — consistent with SIGNED being an omissible default spelling, not a mandatory token.

(7) ADVERSARIAL CHECKS THAT FAILED TO REFUTE. Not reflow, wrapping, hyphenation, or page-break furniture — this is a glyph-level typographic mark inside a single figure. Not a downscaling artifact — confirmed at native 300 dpi by pixel census, not just by eye. Not a misquote — the markdown line matches verbatim. Not a systematic misreading of the whole figure by the transcriber — I checked every other word in the note against the render (USAGE, BINARY, BIT, COMPUTATIONAL, COMP, DISPLAY, the FLOAT-* set, INDEX, MESSAGE-TAG, NATIONAL, OBJECT, REFERENCE, FACTORY, ACTIVE-CLASS, ONLY, PACKED-DECIMAL, NO, SIGN, POINTER, FUNCTION-POINTER, PROGRAM-POINTER all underlined; IS, OF, TO, WITH all unmarked) and every one of them is classified correctly. SIGNED is the single misclassified word, which makes it a specific, isolated, actionable defect rather than noise.

The finding is genuine, normative, and described substantially correctly by the claim.
verdict.corrected_description: The page-533 figure note in specs/ISO_COBOL.md misclassifies SIGNED as a required (underlined) word. In the printed standard, all four USAGE brace groups — BINARY-CHAR, BINARY-SHORT, BINARY-LONG and BINARY-DOUBLE, each followed by { SIGNED / UNSIGNED } — print UNSIGNED with a full-width underline and SIGNED with NO underline (verified at 300 dpi: the UNSIGNED rule measures 0.91 dark fraction across all four rows, while the SIGNED band never exceeds 0.54, that maximum being the glyph baseline itself). SIGNED is therefore an OPTIONAL word per 5.2.3 and 8.9, and by 5.2.6.3 the SIGNED alternative — containing only optional words — is the DEFAULT alternative, implicitly selected unless UNSIGNED is explicitly written. The claim's phrasing that the brace is "satisfiable by writing nothing at all" is correct in effect but is more precisely stated as implicit selection of the default alternative under 5.2.6.3. Consequently `USAGE BINARY-CHAR`, `USAGE BINARY-CHAR SIGNED` and `USAGE BINARY-CHAR UNSIGNED` are all legal and the first two are equivalent (likewise -SHORT, -LONG, -DOUBLE). FIX: move `SIGNED` out of the underlined list in the line-22406 figure note and into the not-underlined list, restating it as "`IS`, `OF`, `TO`, `WITH`, and `SIGNED` are not underlined — they are optional words; the SIGNED alternative contains only optional words and is therefore the default alternative selected when neither SIGNED nor UNSIGNED is written (5.2.6.3)." Two further notes for the fixer: the ASCII figure in the code fence carries no underlining at all, so this note is the only place the required/optional distinction survives in the transcription; and SIGNED is the ONLY misclassified word in the note — every other entry was checked against the render and is correct.
